body.q: Who became the new CEO of Continent 8 in 2026?

results.name: Continent 8 Names Mike Small as New CEO, Founder Michael Tobin Becomes Chairman
results.content:
After 28 years at the helm as CEO, founder Michael Tobin is stepping down from his role but will remain actively involved as the company’s chairman. Mike Small will take over as CEO starting July 15, 2026.
Continent 8 Technologies, a leading provider of IT solutions for online gaming and betting, is undergoing a significant change in its leadership team. After 28 years at the helm as CEO, founder Michael Tobin is stepping down from his role but will remain actively involved as the company’s chairman. Mike Small will take over as CEO starting July 15, 2026.
Small’s background also includes CEO responsibilities for the Americas at Sitel Group along with senior roles at notable firms including IBM, Hewlett Packard, Capgemini, and VXI & SYMBIO Global Solutions. He is already familiar with Continent 8, having served as a strategic board advisor for one year before his promotion.
Michael Tobin will support Small by overseeing governance, strategy, and shareholder relations, ensuring a seamless transition. Tobin expressed pride in Continent 8’s achievements over nearly three decades and emphasized that his decision to step down was carefully planned to maintain the company’s stability.
Tobin stated he has complete confidence in Small’s capabilities, highlighting his experience in scaling global tech businesses and his strong understanding of Continent 8’s customers and strategic goals as reasons he is the right person to lead the company’s next phase.

results.content:
# Africa CEO Forum  
The Africa CEO Forum is the foremost international meeting for African CEOs and investors. They focus on shaping the future of Africa and shaping policies that define the continent's role in global energy markets.
### 1w
🌍 Kigali, 14 & 15 May. 2,800 leaders. Five continents listening.  
Five days after the close of Africa CEO Forum 2026, the voices from the stage are still circulating across the global press.  
In the days that followed, the global financial press analyzed what was said. Pan-African flagships dissected the strategic shifts. Public broadcasters debated the calls to action. International wires carried the headlines from Lagos to Nairobi, from Cairo to Beijing, from Paris to New York.  
Five continents. One story.  
What these newsrooms picked up: a continent that no longer asks for the floor. It takes it.  
"Africa must stop debating its potential and scale up." Paul Kagame.  
"Africa First." Bola Tinubu, calling for a pan-African commodity exchange to cut dollar dependence.  
An African private sector told to scale up, leaders making the case for shared capitalism, the end of the extractive mining model.  
Africa CEO Forum is no longer simply the annual gathering of the African private sector. It is now the place where Africa's economic story is written, from Africa.  
Thank you to the newsrooms and journalists carrying these conversations far beyond Kigali.  
See you in 2027.  
#AfricaCEOForum #ACF2026 #Kigali
